comparison: Both OpenEval and peer reviewers strongly support the genetic association findings (C4, C52-C55). All reviewers praise the multi-ethnic cohort data and statistical rigor. OpenEval additionally evaluates C58-C59 (independence from syndromic scoliosis), which peer reviewers accept implicitly in R11.

Perfect agreement on C10, C95-C97. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the functional validation showing that wild-type COL11A1 restores normal MMP3 expression while the P1335L variant fails to do so. Both acknowledge this as key evidence linking the variant to disease mechanism.

Complete agreement on C15. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the integrative model connecting genetic association, expression studies, regulatory relationships, and estrogen signaling. All reviewers view this as a valuable contribution to understanding AIS pathogenesis.

Strong agreement on C11-C14, C99-C107, C111 regarding estrogen receptor signaling. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the evidence that ESR2 modulates the Col11a1-Mmp3 pathway. OpenEval notes species/cell-type specificity limitations (C108-C110), which peer reviewer R10 acknowledges with uncertainty.

Both support C5-C7 showing PAX1 and collagen XI colocalization and reduction in Pax1-/- mice. Peer reviewer R2 explicitly confirms these immunofluorescence findings. OpenEval notes the quantification is qualitative rather than quantitative.

Both support C76-C79 showing reduced expression of AIS-associated genes (Gpr126, Sox6) in Pax1 mutant mice. Peer reviewer R2 explicitly acknowledges this qRT-PCR data. OpenEval provides broader evaluation including C70-C75 (knockout phenotype, immunofluorescence, RNAseq, GO analysis), which peer reviewers address separately in R12 and R13.

Both support the Col11a1-Mmp3 regulatory relationship (C84-C87, C90). Peer reviewer R2 confirms the finding though misstates 'reduction' instead of 'increase' in MMP3. OpenEval also evaluates C8-C9 (bidirectional regulation), which peer reviewers address in R14.

OpenEval supports C8-C9 showing bidirectional regulation between Pax1 and Col11a1, and Col11a1 and Mmp3. Peer reviewer R4 accepts the overall Pax1-Col11a1-Mmp3 signaling axis, implicitly supporting these regulatory relationships.

Both support C60-C62 showing COL11A1 expression in cartilage by RNAseq. Peer reviewers do not explicitly discuss this but accept it as supporting data. OpenEval also evaluates C63-C68 (immunohistochemistry localization), which peer reviewers address in R9.

Both support C63-C68 showing tissue-specific localization of COL11A1 in IVDs and growth plates. Peer reviewer R2 explicitly acknowledges this immunohistochemistry data. OpenEval also includes C60-C62 (RNAseq) and C118 (collagen XI function), addressed separately by peer reviewers.

Both address C108-C110 showing differential response to Esr2 knockdown in rat CEP cells versus mouse chondrocytes. OpenEval explicitly supports this as evidence of species/cell-type specificity. Peer reviewer R10 marks this as UNCERTAIN, noting the discrepancy was not adequately addressed.
Perfect agreement on C3. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the prior work on PAX1 enhancer association with AIS as foundational context for the current study.

Perfect agreement on C88-C89. Both accept the validation of the Cre system for conditional Col11a1 deletion in cartilage. Peer reviewers note the work 'functionally tests these findings in cell culture and animal models.'

Perfect agreement on C91-C93. Both support the structural location and computational predictions for the P1335L variant. Peer reviewer R1 describes it as 'potentially pathogenic,' consistent with these predictions.

Overlapping evaluation of C71-C73 (immunofluorescence showing PAX1 and collagen XI colocalization). Both support these findings. OpenEval provides comprehensive evaluation of the entire Pax1 knockout experiment (C70-C79), while peer reviewer R2 focuses on the colocalization aspect.

Both support C70 and C74 regarding Pax1 knockout mice phenotype. Peer reviewer R2 acknowledges use of Pax1 knockout model. OpenEval provides more comprehensive evaluation including molecular data (C71-C79).

Both support C75 (gene ontology analysis from Pax1 knockout RNAseq). Peer reviewers do not explicitly discuss this but accept it as supporting ECM-focused interpretation. OpenEval includes this within broader evaluation of Pax1 knockout experiments.

Overlapping evaluation of C99-C100, C104 regarding estrogen receptor effects on Col11a1 and Pax1. Both support these findings. OpenEval provides comprehensive evaluation of the entire estrogen signaling axis (C11-C14, C99-C107, C111), while peer reviewer R14 focuses on specific regulatory relationships.

Both support C86 showing that Col11a1 affects MMP3 expression levels rather than processing. Peer reviewers do not explicitly discuss this mechanistic detail but accept the overall Col11a1-Mmp3 relationship.

Both support C83 showing MMP3 expression in cartilage and bone. Peer reviewers do not explicitly discuss this but accept it as supporting evidence for MMP3 relevance. OpenEval also evaluates C80-C82 (MMP3 function in cancer), addressed in peer R19.

Both support C58-C59 showing the COL11A1 variant is independently associated with AIS rather than syndromic scoliosis. Peer reviewers accept this as important control distinguishing AIS from syndromic mutations. OpenEval includes this within comprehensive genetic association evaluation (R1).

Both support C1-C2, C16-C26 describing established clinical and epidemiological features of AIS. Peer reviewer R19 accepts these as contextual background. OpenEval explicitly evaluates these as literature-supported context claims.

Both support C27-C44, C50-C51 summarizing prior genetic findings in AIS. Peer reviewer R19 accepts these as background context acknowledging the knowledge gap. OpenEval explicitly evaluates these as accurately representing the field's state of knowledge.

Both support C45-C49 summarizing prior animal model studies. Peer reviewer R19 accepts these as contextual background. OpenEval explicitly evaluates these as providing rationale for tissue-specific focus.

Both support C56-C57 describing COL11A1-related syndromes. Peer reviewer R19 accepts this as background context. OpenEval explicitly evaluates this as important for distinguishing AIS-associated variants from syndromic mutations.

Both support C69, C126 describing established Pax1 function. Peer reviewer R19 accepts this as background context. OpenEval explicitly evaluates this as providing developmental context for Pax1 knockout experiments.
Both support C80-C82 describing MMP3 function in cancer biology. Peer reviewer R19 accepts this as background context. OpenEval notes the relevance to AIS requires further validation.

Both support C94 citing precedent for variants affecting gene expression. Peer reviewer R19 accepts this as background context. OpenEval explicitly evaluates this as providing rationale for the observation.

Both support C98 citing rationale for investigating estrogen receptor signaling. Peer reviewer R19 accepts this as background context. OpenEval explicitly evaluates this as supporting the experimental approach.

Both support C112-C120 describing collagen XI structure and function. Peer reviewer R19 accepts these as background context. OpenEval explicitly evaluates these as providing biological context for functional studies.

Both support C121-C125 describing prior COL11A1 associations and functional evidence. Peer reviewer R19 accepts these as background context. OpenEval notes C125 inference would benefit from additional validation.

Both support C127-C129 describing PAX1 and SOX factor relationships. Peer reviewer R19 accepts these as background context. OpenEval notes direct evidence for SOX-mediated Col11a1 regulation is lacking.

OpenEval marks C130-C137 as UNCERTAIN, noting C136-C137 are speculative regarding vSSC differentiation and causal role in AIS. Peer reviewer R19 accepts the background context (C130-C135) but does not explicitly evaluate the speculative claims about mechanism.

Both support C138-C141 describing MMP3 function. Peer reviewer R19 accepts these as background context. OpenEval notes C141 is speculative and the manuscript does not directly test MMP3 enzymatic activity or nuclear translocation.
Both support C142-C144 regarding P1335L variant mechanism. Peer reviewer R19 accepts these as background context. OpenEval notes C144 is speculative and the mechanism remains uninvestigated.

OpenEval marks C145-C146 as UNCERTAIN, noting C146 is speculative regarding collagen XI as mechanoreceptor. Peer reviewer R19 accepts C145 as background context but does not explicitly evaluate the mechanistic speculation.
